newsitem.title: UK: Ford to cut 1300 jobs at UK Halewood plant.
newsitem.headline: Ford to cut 1300 jobs at UK Halewood plant.

text.p: Ford Motor Co intends to cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant on Merseyside, local Member of Parliament David Alton said on Thursday.
Alton, the Liberal Democrat MP for Liverpool Mossley Hill, said he had been told by Ford management this morning that Halewood would operate a single shift as from April.
But, he said the car giant was looking at Halewood as the probable European manufacturing site for a new vehicle -- possibly in the family saloon range.

"I've spoken to Ford this morning and they say that these jobs will be lost through voluntary separation and they've told me that they'll operate on a single shift basis for the foreseeable future, starting in April," Alton told Reuters.

"There's some good news in what they say as well -- that they're looking at Halewood as the probable European site for a planned new vehicle. And althought they won't divulge future product plans, my understanding is that this would be a vehicle somewhere between a Galaxy and a Sierra in size," he added.
The proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to about 3,000 compared with a peak of 14,000 in the 1960s.
Alton said plans to build a new car at Halewood should secure jobs for the 3,000 workers who remain on the site and could even lead to some of the redundant employees being rehired.
One in three people are unemployed on some of the housing estates near the plant and Alton said the news from Ford was a disaster for them.
